newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Tel says intensifying talks on int'l franchise.
newsitem.headline: HK Tel says intensifying talks on int'l franchise.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd chief executive Linus Cheung said on Tuesday the company was entering intense discussions with the government on its international telephone franchise.

Cheung told a news conference there was no pressure on the company to strike a deal giving up its international voice telephone monopoly as both the Hong Kong and Chinese governments had pledged to honour the franchise until it expires in 2006.
But he admitted the increase in callback services was eroding the value of the franchise.
"We knew that it would be eroding the value of the franchise but that does not mean the franchise is worthless. It is a matter of agreeing on a valuation," he said.
"I for one, as chief executive of Hongkong Telecom, would feel very comfortable just sticking to the licence until the year 2006. Unless the price is right there'll be no deal."
Cash would be only one way to compensate the ammendment of the licence and there could be other ways, he said.

Cheung also called on the Hong Kong government's Office of the Telecommunications Authority (OFTA) to allow the company to compete more freely against the three new fixed network telecom service providers and callback operators.

"We have cooperated in creating the conditions for the new network operators to have the equality of opportunity to compete. However, OFTA has yet to adopt a level playing field which would enable us to compete," he said.
Cheung urged OFTA to let Hongkong Telecom have greater freedom to offer lower rates and packages and to rebalance local and international prices.
Hongkong Telecom is about 58 percent owned by Cable and Wireless Plc.
